title: Multiplicative splitting of a Walsh character along XOR
statement:
Let $S \subseteq [n]$, let $f, g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be Boolean functions, and suppose the interchange-of-summation identity
\[
  \sum_{x} \Big(\sum_{y} f(y)\, g(x \oplus y)\Big)\,\chi_S(x)
  \;=\; \sum_{y} f(y) \sum_{x} g(x \oplus y)\,\chi_S(x)
\]
holds, where all sums range over $\{0,1\}^n$ and $\oplus$ is componentwise XOR. Then for all $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$,
\[
  \chi_S(x) \;=\; \chi_S(x \oplus y)\,\chi_S(y),
\]
where $\chi_S$ is the Walsh--Fourier character of $S$; that is, $\chi_S$ is a character of the group $(\bbf_2)^n$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean functions f and g of arity n
the Fubini/interchange-of-summation identity involving f, g and the character (an unused premise)
arbitrary points x, y of the hypercube
caveat: The interchange-of-summation premise is carried by the statement but plays no role in the conclusion (it is a leftover of the enclosing proof); it is included for faithfulness. The functions $f, g$ appear only in that premise.
replaced:
For all $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$ and $S \subseteq [n]$,
\[
  \chi_S(x) \;=\; \chi_S(x \oplus y)\,\chi_S(y),
\]
expressing that $\chi_S$ is a character of the group $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$.  The statement
also carries the (unused) Fubini hypothesis of the enclosing proof.
